title: ProofPath POC sprint lab notebook
content:
One-page working notebook for the ProofPath customer POC. Purpose: single source for sprint milestones, lab/ workshop day plans, live task tracker and a risk ledger to support fast handoffs between SEs and the customer success / infra teams. This is intentionally informal — keep as the mutable truth during the 4-week trial.

Goal summary:
- Validate integrated inference flow for customer’s internal search assistant using Redwood Dedicated and optional Private deployment (VPC).
- Demonstrate latency SLOs (95th p50 target <= 120ms for short queries, p95 <= 350ms for long multi-turn sessions) under representative concurrency.
- Show measurable cost-per-1000-token estimate with and without prefix caching and batching.
- Produce a runbook for quick scale to reserved capacity if the pilot hits production thresholds.

Success criteria (what the customer signs off on):
1) End-to-end demo with their data connector and a seeded prompt set — responses within SLA and <= 6% quality regression vs. baseline model.
2) Predictable cost projection (3 scenarios: low/med/high traffic) in a spreadsheet and agreed gating metric for upgrade to Dedicated.
3) A short ops checklist (5 items) that their infra/ security leads can run to verify Private deployment readiness.
4) A transfer package (Terraform snippet + service account guide + test traffic harness).

Key stakeholders and roles (quick):
- Jordan Reyes (SE, owner) — overall POC lead, workshop facilitator
- Maya Singh (Solutions Eng, metrics + evals) — quality monitoring, prompt set metrics
- Ethan Cole (Infra SE) — Dedicated sizing, autoscaling policy mockups, KMS integration owner
- Priya Raman (Customer Success) — customer liaison, commercial thresholds, acceptance signoff
- Samir Patel (Security) — review of network controls and audit log requirements
- Customer leads: Tara N. (Data platform), Luis M. (Product owner), Dev contact: Anika G.

High-level timeline (4-week sprint) — snapshot as of kickoff:
Week 0 (pre-sprint, days -7 to 0):
- Deliver onboarding checklist + account access (done: invite sent)
- Provide sample Terraform starter (action: Ethan)
- Collect representative prompt set + corpus (action: Tara)
Week 1: Integration & baseline measurements
- Day 1: Kickoff workshop (90m): architecture review, success criteria, env access, test harness handoff.
- Day 2-4: Connector work (customer + SE pair programming) — get request path wired, deploy test endpoint.
- Day 5: Baseline ops run — 1k queries from harness, collect latency/cost/QoE.
Week 2: Optimization experiments
- Implement KV/prefix caching on common user flows. A/B with baseline.
- Try two quantization profiles for cost/latency tradeoff.
- Run 95th percentile load jobs (concurrency ramp to 50 qps).
Week 3: Harden and prepare Private/Dedicated proposal
- Draft Dedicated sizing & autoscale policy doc.
- Smoke test Private VPC route and KMS integration.
- Prepare the cost scenarios and ROI slide.
Week 4: Handoff, acceptance & next steps
- Final demo with customer acceptance checklist.
- Deliver transfer package and runbook.
- Retrospective + go/no-go decision for Dedicated commit.

Daily workshop / lab schedule (sample for Week 1 Day 2):
09:00-09:15 sync: status and blockers (SE + customer devs)
09:15-11:00 pairing: connector auth + sample query path
11:00-12:00 deploy test endpoint to sandbox (SE infra help)
12:00-13:00 lunch (notes: sample data mask script run)
13:00-15:00 profiling: capture p50/p95, token counts; record KV-hit rates
15:00-16:00 calibration: tune batch windows, retry policy
16:00-17:00 wrap: action items and next-step owners

Live task tracker (mutable; checkboxes shorthand):
- [ ] Gather final prompt set (owner: Tara) — due: W0 end
- [x] Create sandbox project + API creds (owner: Jordan) — done 2025-11-03
- [ ] Terraform starter PR (owner: Ethan) — PR#678 in review
- [ ] Build test harness with replay mode (owner: Maya) — target W1 end
- [ ] KV cache experiment (owner: Jordan) — planned W2 day1
- [ ] Quantization test (owner: Ethan) — planned W2 day3
- [ ] Security checklist (owner: Samir) — draft by W3
- [ ] Final acceptance run (owner: Priya + Customer) — W4 day2

Risk ledger (score = likelihood x impact, 1-9):
- Data access delays (score 6): customer legal review of dataset may push connector work. Mitigation: use redacted sample if full data not available. Owner: Tara.
- Network egress constraints (score 4): customer's VPC rules require additional route approvals. Mitigation: temporary tunnel via approved jump host. Owner: Samir.
- Model quality regression (score 5): caching + quantization could increase hallucination for long context. Mitigation: run targeted evals for top 50 prompts and keep fallback policy to full precision model. Owner: Maya.
- Infra surprise under load (score 6): autoscale cooldowns and streambackpressure cause spikes. Mitigation: conservative concurrency cap + synthetic soak run. Owner: Ethan.

Dependencies and blockers (explicit):
- Customer needs to enable service account and provide whitelisted IPs (blocker until W0 end).
- Access to a sample of warm user traffic (preferably anonymized) for caching accuracy testing.
- KMS key admin approval for Private trial (security signoff).

Open questions (to resolve in W0 workshop):
- Which metric will the customer use as the gating threshold for dedicated capacity? (cost per DAU, or p95 latency under X QPS?)
- Is there any PII in the prompts that prevents uploading samples to hosted sandbox? Do we need a local-only run?
- Preferred SLO windows (slower windows allowed at night?)
- Billing-connected owner for cost projection — who will sign the reserved capacity PO if we hit the threshold? (Priya to confirm)

Quick test matrix (what we run during optimization):
- Baseline: FP16 model, no cache, default batcher
- Cache experiment: prefix/KV caching enabled, warm-up run, measure hit-rate and delta in token usage
- QuantizeA: 4-bit quantized variant (fast), compare p95 latency and QA drop
- QuantizeB: mixed-precision hybrid (safer), compare cost/latency
- Fallback policy: if QoE delta > 8% for high-value prompts, route to FP16 model

Notes from Kickoff (2025-11-03 10:00 AM):
- Customer emphasized latency-sensitive user flows (search-as-you-type + clarification turns).
- They have an existing caching layer but inconsistent with conversational context.
- Legal flagged potential export-control items in dataset; Samir to coordinate with their legal.
- Customer prefers a ~2 week trial before budgetary commitment — propose a 2-week deep pilot inside the 4-week POC to evaluate product-market fit.

Deliverables by end of POC (artifact list):
- Performance report (CSV + graphs) with baseline vs experiments
- Cost scenarios spreadsheet (low/med/high) with assumptions and per-1000-token estimates
- Transfer bundle: Terraform snippet, service-account playbook, smoke-test harness (python script + replay dataset)
- Ops checklist (5-step) for Private deployment signoff
- Short exec summary slide (1 page) for commercial/PO decision

Communication plan and cadence:
- Twice-weekly sync (Mon/Wed 30m) during integration phase; ad-hoc deep labs on demand
- Slack channel: #poc-proofpath (customer accepted invite)
- Weekly snapshot email (Priya send Tue EOD) with A/B experiment results and open blockers

Post-POC options presented to customer (to discuss in W4):
- Move to small Dedicated pool (3x A10 equivalent) + SLA for p95 latency; commit term: 6mo
- Private on-prem pilot for regulated dataset — estimate 4 weeks to install and validate
- Hosted with heavier caching layer and higher token-price discount for volume

Retrospective template (what to capture after final demo):
- What worked well (tools/processes)
- Biggest surprises / blockers and root causes
- Who needs to be involved earlier next time
- Concrete improvements to the starter Terraform + onboarding checklist

Action items (immediate):
- Jordan: send out workshop agenda + runbook draft (today)
- Ethan: finish Terraform PR review and add an example autoscale policy (due: 2025-11-06)
- Maya: baseline harness stub (replay style) with embedded eval metrics (due: 2025-11-07)
- Samir: list required approvals for KMS and network (due: 2025-11-05)
- Priya: confirm commercial owner for reserved capacity decision (due: 2025-11-04)

Notes to self (Jordan):
- Keep the demo lean: focus on 2 top user journeys, show a regression guard, and cost delta with/without caching.
- Record lab pairing sessions for onboarding packet.
- Capture all experiment configs in a single yaml under infra repo.

Appendix: quick links and references
- Internal: infra PR (github) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678
- Linear ticket: SE-412 (POC setup)
- Confluence writeup: PROOFPATH-POC-ONBOARD (seeded with checklist)

-- end of notebook (live doc) --

Comments: This file should be used to add checkboxes during the live workshop and to capture short logs of unexpected findings (e.g., "11/05 14:22:  KV hit-rate unexpectedly low on query family X"). Keep free-format entries short and tag owners with initials for quick followups.
